audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Deuteronomy / Devarim Moses-death and Torah-closing witness, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Nebo/Pisgah vision, promised land panorama, Moses' death at Divine mouth, unknown burial place, age and vigor, thirty-day mourning, Joshua's wisdom, Moses' unique prophetic intimacy, and Torah's closing signs-and-deeds witness.

verses.restored: Moses went up from plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, top of Pisgah, which is opposite Jericho. YHWH showed him all land: Gilead as far as Dan,

familiar.text: And Moses went up from the plains of Moab unto the mountain of Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is over against Jericho. And the LORD shewed him all the land of Gilead, unto Dan,

verses.restored: all Naphtali, land of Ephraim and Manasseh, all land of Judah as far as western sea,

familiar.text: And all Naphtali, and the land of Ephraim, and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah, unto the utmost sea,

verses.restored: the Negev and the plain, valley of Jericho, city of palms, as far as Zoar.

familiar.text: And the south, and the plain of the valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees, unto Zoar.

verses.restored: YHWH said to him, This is land I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, To your seed I will give it. I have caused you to see it with your eyes, but there you shall not cross.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto him, This is the land which I sware unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, saying, I will give it unto thy seed: I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither.

verses.restored: Moses, servant of YHWH, died there in land of Moab, at mouth/command of YHWH.

familiar.text: So Moses the servant of the LORD died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the LORD.

verses.restored: He buried him in valley in land of Moab opposite Beth-peor, and no one knows his burial place to this day.

familiar.text: And he buried him in a valley in the land of Moab, over against Bethpeor: but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day.

verses.restored: Moses was one hundred twenty years old when he died; his eye was not dim, and his vigor had not fled.

familiar.text: And Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.

verses.restored: Children of Israel wept for Moses in plains of Moab thirty days; then days of weeping and mourning for Moses were completed.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days: so the days of weeping and mourning for Moses were ended.

verses.restored: Joshua son of Nun was full of spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands upon him; children of Israel listened to him and did as YHWH commanded Moses.

familiar.text: And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the LORD commanded Moses.

verses.restored: No prophet has risen again in Israel like Moses, whom YHWH knew face to face,

familiar.text: And there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face,

verses.restored: for all signs and wonders YHWH sent him to do in land of Egypt to Pharaoh and all his servants and all his land,

familiar.text: In all the signs and the wonders, which the LORD sent him to do in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land,

verses.restored: and for all strong hand and all great awe/terror that Moses did before eyes of all Israel.

familiar.text: And in all that mighty hand, and in all the great terror which Moses shewed in the sight of all Israel.

translation_notes: The Torah ends outside the land, with vision rather than possession. Promise remains larger than the lifespan of its greatest leader.

Moses dies 'at the mouth of YHWH,' a phrase that later Jewish tradition beautifully receives as death by a Divine kiss; the restored layer preserves the Hebrew idiom without imposing one interpretation.
The unknown grave prevents possession of Moses' body and keeps the narrative from turning his burial place into a royal monument.
Verse 7 praises preserved sight and vigor at advanced age but must not imply that disability, frailty, dementia, or illness diminishes a person's dignity or spiritual completion.
Thirty days of communal mourning honor grief as a bounded public practice rather than weakness.
Joshua's wisdom is connected to Moses' laying on of hands, while the people remain responsible for listening and action.
The claim that no prophet arose like Moses is Torah's internal affirmation of his unique face-to-face relationship; it must not be used for interreligious contempt.
The final phrase 'before all Israel' closes Torah in communal sight and memory, not private esoteric possession.
safety_note: Do not use Deuteronomy 34 to shame aging, illness, disability, grief, or leaders who cannot complete every vision within one lifetime. Do not turn Moses' uniqueness into contempt for later prophets or religions. Center dignified death, communal mourning, non-dynastic succession, wisdom transmitted by touch, and a sacred work that continues beyond its founder.
